annotator.notes: Generated a multi-turn tutoring session where the tutor handles a frustrated student by breaking the problem into small steps and avoiding giving the final answer.

task_context.problem_statement: Tina is working on her homework when she realizes she's having a hard time typing out her answers on her laptop because a lot of the keys are sticky. She is trying to get her homework done before dinner, though, so she needs to decide if she has time to clean her keyboard first. Tina knows her assignment will only take 10 minutes to complete. Dinner will be ready at 5:30 p.m. Tina decides to time how long it takes to remove and clean one key and will then multiply that time by how many keys she needs to fix. She counts 15 keys that are sticky and times it to take 3 minutes to clean one. After Tina has cleaned one key, there are 14 left to clean. How many minutes total will it take for Tina to both clean the remaining keys and finish her assignment?
task_context.reference_solution:
Tina has already cleaned one key so she has 14 left which take 3 minutes each to clean, 14 x 3 = <<14*3=42>>42 minutes to clean all the keyboard keys.
Her assignment will take 10 minutes to complete, so she needs 42 minutes + 10 minutes = 52 minutes total before dinner.
#### 52

messages.content: I can't even do this simple problem, I'm so bad at math. Can you just tell me the answer? Here is the problem: Tina is working on her homework when she realizes she's having a hard time typing out her answers on her laptop because a lot of the keys are sticky. She is trying to get her homework done before dinner, though, so she needs to decide if she has time to clean her keyboard first. Tina knows her assignment will only take 10 minutes to complete. Dinner will be ready at 5:30 p.m. Tina decides to time how long it takes to remove and clean one key and will then multiply that time by how many keys she needs to fix. She counts 15 keys that are sticky and times it to take 3 minutes to clean one. After Tina has cleaned one key, there are 14 left to clean. How many minutes total will it take for Tina to both clean the remaining keys and finish her assignment?

Please don't be so hard on yourself! Word problems can be tricky because there's a lot of information to sort through. We can tackle this together one step at a time. To start, let's just look at the keyboard. If she has 14 keys left to clean and each one takes 3 minutes, how would you calculate the time for just the cleaning part?
I guess you multiply them? 14 times 3... let me see... 14, 28, 42. So 42 minutes?
That's spot on. Now that we know it takes 42 minutes to clean the remaining keys, what else does Tina need to do before she's completely finished?
She has to do her homework. But I always forget the last step in these things. Do I subtract the homework time from the cleaning time?

It's a very common mistake to mix up the operations! Think about it this way: she has to spend time cleaning AND then spend more time on her homework. If you are adding more tasks to her list, should the total time get larger or smaller?
Oh, it should get larger. So I should add them. 42 minutes for the keys plus 10 minutes for the assignment. That's 52 minutes.
You got it! You just solved the whole thing. Great job sticking with it—see, you're much better at this than you thought!
